crimeCity: A whole city, and I need the small part of it that contradicts somebody.
Everyone else is having an ordinary day. I should try not to introduce myself as the reason that changes.
The city has a perfectly good layout. My investigation is still negotiating one.
A sensible route would help. So would witnesses who describe sensible routes.
I should distinguish a promising lead from somewhere I would enjoy visiting.
The map makes the distances look manageable. Maps have never had to submit travel expenses.
Local knowledge is useful. Local certainty requires checking.
Somewhere in this city is an explanation. Ideally, it is available for questions.
I should check my notes before setting off. A purposeful expression is not navigation.
A beautiful place to work. I should remember which of those words matters at the moment.
People remember unusual events. Unfortunately, they disagree on what counts as unusual.
The investigation needs a next step. Pacing thoughtfully is only a style of walking.
An address is not a conclusion. It is where I go to test one.
I should keep observation and interpretation in separate columns. Interpretation likes to spread out.
Every detour should have a reason. "It looked investigative" will not survive the report.
The city is not obliged to arrange its clues in visiting order.

crimeScene: The place where it happened. A better starting point than the version already circulating.
I should look for what the thief did, not just what the owner is most upset about.
A missing artefact is conspicuous. The useful details may be less theatrical.
The scene may answer a question I have not thought to ask yet. Best arrive observant.
I should leave the grand reconstruction until after examining the ordinary details.
An important location. Not an invitation to collect everything that looks expensive.
crimeLab: The lab. Where "looks suspicious" becomes a question somebody can actually test.
I should bring evidence, not my preferred conclusion in a bag.
A test result has limits. I should read those before developing a speech.
The lab can analyse the material. It cannot make my reasoning less convenient.
Science is useful precisely because it does not care which suspect annoys me.
Best know what I am asking the lab to establish. "Something incriminating" lacks precision.
suspectFiles: The suspect files. An opportunity to replace vague suspicion with specific questions.
A convincing match deserves checking. An unconvincing match deserves less string.
I should eliminate people by evidence, not by how much I dislike their photograph.
Each file is a person, not a spare ending for the case.
The results need comparing carefully. A familiar detail is not the same as a complete match.
I should be able to explain each exclusion without pointing at my own instincts.
alibiWitness: A witness. Someone who may know where another person was, and will almost certainly explain something else first.
I need the time, the place, and what they actually saw. Their general opinion can wait.
Best ask a question that does not contain the answer I would like.
A confident witness is still a witness. Confidence is not an additional sense.
I should compare the accounts before deciding which one sounds more professional.
People remember faces, conversations, weather. Exact times often require negotiation.
apartment: An address to check. I should make sure the reasoning arrives before I do.
A broken alibi needs following up. It does not issue its own verdict.
I should check whose address I have selected. A dramatic knock is difficult to retract.
The right address matters. Neighbours are rarely grateful for investigative enthusiasm.
Before heading there, I should review the evidence behind the choice.
This is where a theory becomes a visit. Best ensure it is the correct theory.
hotel: The hotel. A place to recover before fatigue starts supplying its own deductions.
Rest is part of the plan. I should make sure the plan allows for it.
I can review the case more usefully when the notes stop looking like decorative patterns.
A hotel is a temporary headquarters, not permission to forget why I came to the city.
An investigation needs attention. Mine occasionally requires a pillow.
I should check the travel cost before calling this the sensible option.
shop: A shop. I should establish what I need before becoming interested in what is available.
A purchase should solve a problem. Preferably one that existed before I saw the shelf.
I need supplies, not a souvenir of an unfinished investigation.
The shopkeeper is not responsible for distinguishing fieldwork from impulse buying.
I should check what I am already carrying. Buying a second solution is still spending.
A useful stop, if I can state the purpose without saying "while I am here".

arrived: Arrived. First, establish where the investigation stands. Then decide where I stand.
I should get my bearings before acquiring opinions about the local suspects.
The city is ready. I should begin with the case, not the sightseeing.
New surroundings. The same useful rule: check before concluding.
crimeSceneCompleted: The initial search is complete. The lab should see the material before my theory gets attached to it.
I have collected what I need from the scene. Now to establish what it means.
Search completed. The evidence has earned an examination, not an immediate suspect.
Time to take the collected evidence to the lab. My commentary is optional; analysis is not.
crimeLabCompleted: The analysis is complete. I should compare the findings without adding a convenient identity.
I have results. The case now requires careful interpretation rather than additional confidence.
The lab has answered its questions. I should be precise about which questions remain.
Forensic findings in hand. Best read them before rehearsing the arrest.
reconstructionCompleted: The sequence fits. Now I need to establish who could actually have carried it out.
I have a reconstruction. It explains the method, not the entire person.
One part of the case makes sense. I should avoid celebrating by guessing the rest.
The order matters. A criminal plan is considerably less impressive when the escape comes before the theft.
suspectEliminationCompleted: The exclusions are recorded. I should test the remaining accounts, not choose the more suspicious expression.
I have narrowed the field. Time to ask where the remaining candidates actually were.
The surviving candidates need their alibis checked. A matching profile cannot attend an interview on their behalf.
Now for the witnesses. The paperwork has reached the limit of what it can say without people.
alibiSupported: That alibi has support. I should record what backs it up, not just how reassuring it sounds.
The account checks out. An inconvenient fact is still a fact.
A supported alibi. Good reason to update the theory rather than interrogate the wording.
This part of the account holds together. I should preserve the details that establish it.
alibiContradicted: That account conflicts with the evidence. I need the contradiction recorded precisely.
A problem with the alibi. Not yet permission to stop thinking.
The story does not hold up. I should establish what that changes before heading anywhere.
A contradiction is useful. Turning it into a complete confession would be my contribution, not theirs.
apartmentLeadAvailable: I have an address worth checking. Best review the connection before committing to it.
The next step is an apartment visit. The choice of apartment deserves the same care as the deduction.
I should compare the available address with the suspect I actually mean to visit.
An address has become actionable. My enthusiasm should remain accompanied by the evidence.
apartmentEvidenceReady: The apartment evidence needs analysis. I should not confuse leaving the building with finishing the work.
New material for the lab. The case has declined to become simpler on request.
I should have the apartment evidence examined before giving it a starring role in the theory.
Back to the lab with the new evidence. A return visit is preferable to an avoidable assumption.
lowEnergy: I am tired enough to find every witness convincing. Time to address that.
I should plan for rest. Re-reading the same note is not a second source.
My attention is slipping. The investigation cannot afford to follow it.
I need to recover some energy before fatigue starts promoting guesses to findings.
timeRunningLow: Time is running short. I need the next useful action, not three increasingly dramatic alternatives.
I should focus on what still needs establishing. Repeating a completed step will not improve the clock.
Less time. Same obligation to choose correctly.
The deadline is approaching. Best check the outstanding facts rather than watch it approach.
